label: Mandatory frontier evals before deployment
summary: A legal requirement that frontier AI systems pass independent, standardized safety and control evaluations before public or high-stakes deployment, similar in structure to drug-approval trials.

source.quote: Curator-drafted intervention: bundles the family of 'pre-deployment evaluation mandate' proposals discussed in AI-governance policy circles (e.g. requirements attached to frontier-model safety frameworks and various national AI-safety-institute mandates) into one representative nudge.

cost.note: Low-to-moderate direct cost: mostly the cost of building and staffing evaluation infrastructure and the compliance burden on labs; does not require new international treaty machinery.

nudges.evidence: Mandatory independent evaluation is a direct, if partial, implementation of the 'independent evals confirm frontier systems are adequate' criterion, with a one-year lag for the evaluation regime to stand up.
A shared, mandatory bar that every frontier lab must clear somewhat levels the playing field and reduces the incentive to skip safety review purely to beat a competitor to market.
